overview: This table tells the game which traps to prepare for each character before a battle.
description: Per-character lists of trap Blueprint asset names collected by the shared retail trap asset collector during battle preparation and battle preload; this table holds asset selection, not per-trap tuning data.

ID.simple: The name of this trap list. The game uses it to match the list to the right character.
ID.technical: FName FGameDataTableRow_CharacterTrap::Id at row+0x08 behind the 8-byte FTableRowBase; the export writes it as ID while ImportKeyField is Id. All five exported rows have ID equal to their row key (CP_130, CP_140, CP_150, CN_122, CN_250), and each is referenced once by CharacterDataTable::Id_CharacterTrap; the second trap-ID slot is None in each referencing character. BattleAssets_Traps_12BCE80 skips None trap IDs and resolves each remaining ID with FindRow<FGameDataTableRow_CharacterTrap>(Id, TEXT(""), false) over CharacterTrapDataTables (DTM +0x4C0), taking the first non-null matching row without a missing-row warning. The stored Id value is not otherwise read by the observed consumers; no Blueprint-only reader can be confirmed from the available evidence.

FileName_BP.simple: Which traps the game gets ready for this character before a battle. Change the names to change which traps are ready.
FileName_BP.technical: TArray<FName> at row+0x10; the constructor leaves it empty, so every exported value comes from data. Each of the five exported rows serializes exactly ten positional slots with no per-index behavior: 13 non-None names and 37 None entries in total. BattleAssets_Traps_12BCE80 appends the entire array for every resolved trap row, including None entries, unlike the None trap-ID filter; GamePrimaryAssetLoader_CreateLoaders then skips None names and duplicate asset names and keeps the first occurrence when building the GamePrimaryAssetType_Trap loader map. These are FName asset names, not trap row IDs, and no statistics, sockets, spawn rules or units are stored. All 13 exported names match FileName_BP values in TrapDataTable (TR_010_00_BP is shared by TR_010_00/_01/_02 and TR_032_00_BP comes from TR_030_00), but no code joins the two tables. The collector has two direct call sites: battle prepare collects TrapNames into StudioTrapLoaders_860, and battle preload collects Names into StudioTrapLoaders_2C0; both maps are later merged into StudioRetainedLoaders_90. The level-sequencer path creates an empty TrapNames list and does not read this table. Missing CharacterTrap rows contribute nothing. Runtime spawning independently reads TrapDataTable's own FileName_BP through AGameTrapManager::SpawnPooled and the same Trap primary asset type; that shared asset identity is an indirect relationship, not a read of this row.

notes: Export contains exactly one CharacterTrapDataTable asset with 5 rows; every row has ten FileName_BP slots, of which 13 are populated and 37 are None. The None asset entries are passed to the loader builder but discarded there.

Distinct from TrapDataTable (DTM +0x670), which supplies trap rows, ActionType and spawn asset names to gameplay controllers and AGameTrapManager. The CharacterTrap collector does not read TrapDataTable or ActionType; the two converge only on Trap primary asset names.

Lookup precedence is first non-null row in CharacterTrapDataTables in array order; only the single 'CharacterTrapDataTable' loader is registered in this export/build (DTM +0x4C0), after all DataTable loaders complete. The resulting trap loaders are retained in UGamePhase::StudioRetainedLoaders_90 on phase exit.

The collector is recorded as a byte MATCH at retail RVA 0x12bce80 in status/verdicts.json; loader/cache and spawn contexts are reconstructed C++ with retail RVA comments. Retail Blueprint graphs and cooked assets were not available, so Blueprint-only consumers cannot be excluded.

usages.detail: Resolves the single 'CharacterTrapDataTable' primary asset into AGameDataTableManager::CharacterTrapDataTables (+0x4C0).
Registers 'CharacterTrapDataTable' in the DataTable primary-asset name list.
BattleAssets_Traps_12BCE80 resolves Character::Id_CharacterTrap entries and appends FileName_BP to the caller's name array.
Battle prepare state 1 collects trap names for the StudioTrapLoaders_860 map built at line 296.
Battle preload collects trap names for the StudioTrapLoaders_2C0 map built at line 306.
StudioTrapLoaders_2C0 is appended to StudioRetainedLoaders_90 on phase exit; the battle-prepare map is retained in GamePhase_BattleBase.cpp:1073.
Indirect asset-name convergence: spawn-time traps are resolved from TrapDataTable FileName_BP through the same Trap primary asset type, not from this table.
